description: ## Goal Extend `Filament.Test` with two functions for Rung 3 tests that use a real (test-started) observable GenServer instead of a stub: - `update/1` — drain pending observable update messages and re-render - `eventually/2` — retry an assertion with a timeout (for async observable delivery) Rung 3 is for testing that a component correctly reacts to observable state changes. The component and the observable both run in the test process (no separate node needed). ## Deviation policy Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run `bw comment "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await guidance. Do not improvise. --- ## Prerequisite F1 merged — `Filament.Test` struct and mount/3 must exist. --- ## 1. Filament.Test.update/1 FILE: test/support/filament_test.ex (or wherever F1 placed the module) (add to existing Filament.Test module) Drains all pending Filament messages from the test process mailbox and re-renders. Returns an updated `view`. ```elixir @doc """ Drain pending Filament update messages and re-render. Call this after triggering an observable update to process the resulting {:filament_observable_update, ...} messages that arrive in the test process mailbox. Returns the updated view (re-rendered with new state). Example: CounterServer.increment(server) view = Filament.Test.update(view) assert render_text(view) =~ "Count: 1" """ @spec update(t()) :: t() def update(%__MODULE__{} = view) do flush_messages(view) end ``` NOTE: `flush_messages/1` is already defined in F1 — it drains `:filament_set_state`, `:filament_observable_update`, and `:filament_observable_resubscribe` messages with `after 0` (non-blocking). `update/1` is simply a public alias. Confirm that `flush_messages/1` is exported or accessible from this addition; if it is private, either make it public or duplicate the logic. --- ## 2. Filament.Test.eventually/2 FILE: same file as update/1 ```elixir @doc """ Assert that `assertion_fn.()` returns a truthy value within `timeout` milliseconds. Retries every `interval` ms. Raises ExUnit.AssertionError on timeout. The assertion function must be a zero-arity function. For assertions that need to first call update/1, include that call inside the fn. Example — with explicit update: Filament.Test.eventually(fn -> view = Filament.Test.update(view) render_text(view) =~ "Count: 5" end, timeout: 500) Example — observable delivering in background: spawn(fn -> Enum.each(1..5, fn _ -> CounterServer.increment(counter) end) end) Filament.Test.eventually(fn -> view = Filament.Test.update(view) render_text(view) =~ "Count: 5" end) """ @spec eventually(assertion_fn :: (-> term()), opts :: keyword()) :: :ok def eventually(assertion_fn, opts \\ []) do timeout = Keyword.get(opts, :timeout, 1_000) interval = Keyword.get(opts, :interval, 50) deadline = System.monotonic_time(:millisecond) + timeout do_eventually(assertion_fn, deadline, interval, timeout) end defp do_eventually(fun, deadline, interval, original_timeout) do if fun.() do :ok else remaining = deadline - System.monotonic_time(:millisecond) if remaining <= 0 do raise ExUnit.AssertionError, message: "Filament.Test.eventually/2 timed out after #{original_timeout}ms" else Process.sleep(min(interval, remaining)) do_eventually(fun, deadline, interval, original_timeout) end end end ``` IMPORTANT: `eventually/2` does NOT take a `view` argument because the assertion function needs to call `update/1` itself to get a fresh view. Passing `view` into `eventually` and mutating it would require the view to be in a mutable container (Agent, etc.) which is unnecessary complexity. The documented pattern is: capture `view` in the closure and call `update/1` inside the fn. However, if the user closes over a `view` binding without rebinding, the view won't update between retries. The docs must make this clear: the closure must call `update(view)` and use the returned value for the assertion, not the outer `view` variable. Document this pattern prominently in the @doc. --- ## 3. Tests FILE: test/filament/test/rung3_test.exs Define a test observable (real GenServer using Filament.Observable.GenServer): ```elixir defmodule TestCounter do use Filament.Observable.GenServer def start_link(n), do: GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, n) def init(n), do: {:ok, n} def increment(pid), do: GenServer.call(pid, :increment) def handle_call(:increment, _from, n) do new_n = n + 1 notify_observers(new_n) {:reply, :ok, new_n} end end defmodule CountingComp do use Filament.Component defcomponent do prop :server, :term, required: true def render(assigns) do count = use_observable(@server) ~F[Count: {count}] end end end ``` Test cases: 1. **update/1 processes pending message** — mount CountingComp with real TestCounter (pass pid as prop), call TestCounter.increment, call update(view), assert "Count: 1" 2. **update/1 is idempotent with empty mailbox** — call update(view) with no pending messages, assert returned view is functionally identical (no crash, same HTML) 3. **eventually/2 passes when condition met** — mount, spawn increment in background after short delay, call eventually with assertion that count is 1 4. **eventually/2 raises on timeout** — mount, do NOT increment, call eventually with timeout: 100 expecting count=1, assert ExUnit.AssertionError raised 5. **multiple increments before update** — call increment 3 times, call update once, assert count shows the latest value (3), not an intermediate value Run: `mix test test/filament/test/rung3_test.exs` --- ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `Filament.Test.update/1` exported - [ ] `Filament.Test.eventually/2` exported - [ ] All 5 tests pass - [ ] Dialyzer clean - [ ] F1 tests still pass (no regressions)
title: F2: Rung 3 — update/1 and eventually/2 for real-observable subtree tests
